title: What to do with the side model that went 28-44
option_a: A: Scrap the side entirely and originate only total and moneyline.
option_b: B: Replace the points-based rating with an opponent-adjusted rating (e.g. per-play efficiency) and backtest the replacement on weeks 5-9.
option_c: C: Keep the side, publish its record prominently, and treat it as a documented control.
recommended: B, with C's transparency as a permanent feature of the page.
rationale: The current method averages points for and against with no opponent adjustment, so it double-counts schedule strength. B is the only option that could fix the mechanism rather than hide it. C alone leaves a harmful number in the catalog.

title: What stake schedule should ROI assume
option_b: B: Flat 1 unit at the model's own fair price, i.e. break-even evaluation only.
option_c: C: A fractional-Kelly schedule driven by the model's edge.
recommended: A stays as the headline, B is added as a second column.
rationale: C depends on a calibrated edge, and no edge is measurable without a market line (NM-F01). Shipping Kelly now would produce confident-looking numbers from an unmeasured quantity.

title: Define what counts as a forward bet for gate G09
option_a: A: Any game unplayed when the model line was written, recorded with a UTC timestamp.
option_b: B: Only bets the owner actually placed.
option_c: C: Any game from a season week after the gate-set freeze date.
rationale: A is the only definition that is both mechanical and independent of the owner's behaviour, so the gate cannot be opened by reclassifying backtest rows.

title: Close the 30-club depth-chart gap
option_a: A: Probe all 32 club domains for a depth chart and capture every one that exists.
option_b: B: Capture only the clubs in the current week's slate.
option_c: C: Leave it at two clubs and label it an illustration.
rationale: The deficiency signal is worthless as a two-club anecdote. B is cheaper but creates a rotating coverage gap that makes week-over-week comparison impossible.

title: Choose the push convention
option_a: A: Exclude pushes from the denominator (current).
option_b: B: Count a push as half a loss.
option_c: C: Count a push as a refunded stake, i.e. 0 units but n+1.
recommended: A for the hit rate, C for the units column.
rationale: A and C together are what a reader intuitively expects: the push is not a win and not a loss. B quietly biases every ROI downward.

title: Decide the publication ceiling under the NFL terms
option_a: A: Publish aggregate findings and keep the compiled CSVs private.
option_b: B: Publish everything as a non-commercial informational archive.
option_c: C: Seek written consent from the NFL before publishing the tables.
rationale: The terms permit personal non-commercial informational use but prohibit systematic retrieval to build a database absent consent. A keeps the useful conclusions public while keeping the compiled database private, which is the lowest-risk reading.

title: Add a weekly diff report
option_a: A: A page that diffs this week's numbers against last week's and highlights every change.
rationale: The most decision-relevant fact each week is what changed. Git history exists but nobody reads it while deciding.

title: Resolve the missing-price dead end
option_a: A: Accept blank prices permanently and never claim a market edge.
option_b: B: Add one licensed operator feed, named and dated, as an explicit exception to the official-only rule.
option_c: C: Use a public closing-line archive, clearly marked non-official.
recommended: A now; B only if the owner is willing to change the project's own rule in writing.
rationale: Every other choice here is blocked by the missing price. The owner should decide this first, because it determines whether the whole exercise can ever produce an edge.
